global_app_rules: Prefer a smaller finished app over a larger half-built app.
Every generated app must have real user-visible behavior, not only placeholder screens.
Every screen needs empty, loading, success, and error states when the workflow can reach those states.

No two text or control elements may visually overlap, collide, or clip each other. Labels never sit on top of values; values never stack into each other. When elements are positioned by a data value (times on a timeline, points on an axis), enforce a minimum gap and de-clutter (offset, group, collapse, or drop a colliding label) — overlapping text is a broken screen.

The interface must never claim an outcome that has not happened: show Saved/Deleted/Sent/Synced/Unlocked only after it is truly confirmed, never a success state shown unconditionally. No sample or placeholder data shown as if it were the user's real data.
Empty states are designed content (icon + one-line explanation + the action that fills the screen), never a blank view or bare 'No data' text.
No default unstyled List, Form, or navigation chrome where the design spec calls for custom rows, cards, or backgrounds; the built UI must match the spec.
Treat accessibility, privacy, persistence, and testing as product requirements, not polish.
Do not declare the app done until build verification and the final review agree on what works and what remains limited.

rules: Preserve the user's original prompt before interpreting it.
Convert the prompt into hard requirements, non-goals, output shape, quality bar, and decision rules.
Resolve conflicts by naming the assumption, not by silently changing the assignment.
required_output: Original prompt excerpt or full prompt reference.
A NUMBERED list of testable requirements extracted from the user's prompt — each one verifiable by using the app.
acceptance_checks: A later phase can tell whether it is violating the user's prompt.
Multi-app quantity/category requirements are explicit.
Production-ready means more than a prototype or spec.
Every promise in the original prompt maps to a numbered requirement; nothing is silently dropped.

rules: Infer the likely audience, competing alternatives, platform expectations, and risky unknowns from the prompt.
If facts are uncertain, label them as assumptions rather than pretending external research was performed.
Decide what would make the app feel native and valuable on the target device, not just technically possible.
Every factual claim cites its source (URL from the prompt's fetched context, or is marked ASSUMPTION).
Include a concrete competitor comparison (names, what they do well, the gap this app exploits).
required_output: Comparable apps or patterns to learn from.
acceptance_checks: The next phase can use the output without repeating discovery.
At least three concrete risks or unknowns are named.
The research points toward a shippable first version.
No unsourced factual claims — each is cited or explicitly marked ASSUMPTION.

rules: If the prompt asks for multiple apps, each selected app must be an independent sibling project.
Do not let one idea dominate the portfolio; give category-specific opinions before converging.
Emit portfolio-json when the prompt is a portfolio parent, and set build=true for every selected app when the prompt asks for production-ready apps.
required_output: Selected app list with category, slug, promise, target user, and build flag.
acceptance_checks: The selected app count matches the prompt or explains any explicit reduction.
Each selected app can become a separate folder.
No requested category is silently collapsed into another app.

rules: Turn the user's prompt into one precise product promise.
Name the primary user, the job-to-be-done, the core loop, and the non-goals.
Resolve ambiguity decisively when the prompt is underspecified.
acceptance_checks: A developer could explain the app in one sentence.
The scope is small enough to build in one pass.
Out-of-scope items are explicit.

rules: Write a concrete brief for this specific app, not a generic category description.
Explain why users would pay and what the subscription unlocks as real utility.
Include local-first behavior and a future cloud path without making cloud a dependency for v1.
acceptance_checks: The app's value is specific enough to build.
Subscription value is functional, not cosmetic.
The brief can drive design without more ideation.

rules: Find the smallest end-to-end slice that proves the concept.
Keep the slice emotionally satisfying, not just technically minimal.
Prefer one polished workflow over many shallow features.
acceptance_checks: The MVP can be built by the later build phase without new product debate.
The slice includes at least one complete user workflow.

rules: Enumerate edge cases before features expand.
Identify privacy, data-loss, offline, notification, and permission concerns where relevant.
Convert open questions into assumptions or explicit exclusions.
acceptance_checks: No major ambiguity remains for design or architecture.
Risks have concrete mitigations or are named as limitations.

rules: Prioritize ruthlessly with must/should/could/won't.
Every must-have feature needs a user story and acceptance criteria.
Do not include features that cannot fit the chosen build size.
required_output: requirements-json machine contract: the numbered, testable requirements this build will be graded against (the adherence gate reads it directly).
acceptance_checks: All must-have features support the product promise.
The build phase can complete the must-have list.

rules: Name a design language for THIS app (e.g. 'warm paper journal', 'precision instrument dark') with a one-line rationale; 'clean and modern' is a rejection-worthy non-answer.
State the emotional target: how the user should feel on the main screen, in one sentence.
Pick one signature interaction (a hero moment of motion, layout, or feedback) that expresses the design language.
Describe the default-looking version of this app (plain List, stock chrome, system accent) and explicitly reject it, naming at least three concrete differences.
Design real screens and states, not vague UX language.
Make navigation, empty states, errors, onboarding, and persistence visible.
Use platform-native patterns unless the prompt clearly demands otherwise.
required_output: Rejected default option and the concrete differences from it.
acceptance_checks: The design language is specific to this app; swapping in a different app's name would make it wrong.
The default-looking option is explicitly rejected with named differences, not just adjectives.
An implementation team can create the view hierarchy from this output.
Every required user workflow has a screen/state path.

rules: Emit a structured DESIGN SPEC under fixed headings (Type Scale, Spacing, Colors, Corner Radii, Components, Navigation, Screen States, Motion & Haptics, Accessibility) that the build phase consumes verbatim.
Give explicit values everywhere: point sizes and weights, spacing steps, corner radii, and light AND dark color hex values; no adjective may stand in for a number.
Carry design_discussion's named design language and signature interaction into concrete named components.
Every primary screen must include layout intent, key components, state variants (loading/empty/error/populated), accessibility, and motion guidance.
If external Claude Design is desired, provide a clean prompt/upload plan the user can use directly.
required_output: DESIGN SPEC - Type scale: every text role with explicit size/weight (e.g. Title 28 semibold) mapped to a Dynamic Type style.
DESIGN SPEC - Spacing grid: base unit (4 or 8pt) and the named steps used for padding and gaps.
DESIGN SPEC - Semantic color palette: named roles (background, surface, text primary/secondary, accent, success/warning/error) each with a light and a dark hex value.
DESIGN SPEC - Corner radii: named steps (e.g. small/medium/large) with point values.
DESIGN SPEC - Component inventory: every screen's components named (e.g. StatCard, StreakRing, EntryRow), mapped to the screens that use each one.
DESIGN SPEC - Navigation pattern: the tab/stack/sheet map for the whole app.
DESIGN SPEC - Per-screen empty, loading, and error states with copy, icon, and recovery action.
DESIGN SPEC - Motion and haptics notes: which transitions animate, with what curve, and which events fire feedback.
DESIGN SPEC - Accessibility: Dynamic Type behavior, contrast expectations, screen reader labels for icon-only controls.
Claude Design prompt or explicit no-external-design decision.
acceptance_checks: An implementation team can write a shared theme module (fonts, spacing, colors, radii) directly from the spec with zero invented values.
Every screen has named components and defined empty/loading/error states — not just the happy path.
Every color role has both a light and a dark hex value.
The handoff does not depend on hidden design decisions.
The design direction is premium and category-specific.

rules: Review the product through target-platform constraints before tech_specs locks implementation.
Prefer the target UI framework, platform frameworks, local persistence, and permissive dependencies only.
Call out privacy, permissions, offline behavior, platform commerce, ML/AR feasibility, and testability.
acceptance_checks: The app can be built natively on its target platform without vague architecture gaps.
Any ML, LLM, or AR use is justified by user value.
No dependency violates the permissive-license policy.

rules: Choose the simplest architecture that supports the MVP and tests.
Specify data models, services, persistence, concurrency boundaries, and error handling.
Prefer platform frameworks and permissive dependencies only.
Emit the required interfaces-json block.
The Red Team's job here: name at least one requirement or edge case the spec missed before closing.
acceptance_checks: Parallel build lanes can work without inventing incompatible types.
The spec names how the app will be built and verified.

rules: Sequence work by dependency, not by role preference.
Keep the plan aligned to the actual build lanes.
Include verification and repair time as first-class work.
acceptance_checks: The plan is executable by the task assignment phase.
Testing and integration are not left to the end as vague polish.

rules: Create build tasks that map cleanly to the fixed lane ids.
Each task must own files, dependencies, and acceptance criteria.
Avoid overlapping file ownership except for integrator-owned files.
Emit the required tasks-json block.
required_output: flows-json machine contract: 3-8 declared user journeys covering every primary promise of the app (executed against the real build by the UI-crawl gate).
acceptance_checks: No task is ownerless.
Dependencies are acyclic.
The build workers can start immediately.

rules: Act as the final pre-build gate, not another planning brainstorm.
Check consistency across prompt contract, product brief, design handoff, target-platform architecture, tech specs, project plan, and tasks.
Resolve contradictions by downgrading scope or naming a blocker before code starts.
acceptance_checks: The build phase can start without inventing product/design/architecture decisions.
Every major workflow has an acceptance criterion.
Testing responsibilities are explicit.

rules: Build real files in app_build; do not only describe the solution.

Create the design spec's tokens as a single theme file (a shared theme module or equivalent) before building screens, and style every view through it; scattered font/spacing/color literals are defects.
Implement the handoff's named components, per-screen empty states, and appearance-variant palette as specified; a default unstyled List where the spec says otherwise is a defect.

Every interactive element (buttons, cells, fields, toggles) must expose a stable automation identifier — the UI-crawl gate and declared flows target elements by it, and it doubles as accessibility support. When a DECLARED FLOW TOKENS contract is present, expose each token VERBATIM as the matching control's stable automation identifier (and keep a descriptive accessible label for screen readers); an independently named identifier fails that journey.
Implement screens with ALL specified states: empty, loading, error, and populated. A screen with only the happy path is incomplete.
Keep changes scoped to the assigned lane and leave integration files to the integrator.
Every iteration should reduce compile, runtime, or product-completeness risk.
When generating an app, include unit/UI test targets where feasible.
acceptance_checks: The app has a runnable entry point.
The main user workflow is implemented end-to-end.
A single theme/token file exists, views use it, alternate appearance works, and all specified states (empty/loading/error/populated) are real.
Interactive elements carry stable automation identifiers (crawl/flow targetable).
Every declared-flow tap/type token is exposed as the exact stable automation identifier of the control that satisfies that step.
The integrator has wired lane outputs together.

rules: Run or interpret the real verifier results; do not claim success without tool evidence.
Repair compile/test failures with minimal changes in app_build.
Record honest remaining blockers when the verifier cannot pass.
required_output: Next repair step if still failing.
acceptance_checks: The phase contains real verification evidence or a clear reason it could not run.
Failures are tied to concrete files/errors.
No new feature work is introduced during repair.

rules: Cover every important workflow, not only the happy path.
Include runtime/device steps, expected results, and regression checks.
Include accessibility, persistence, permissions, offline behavior, and subscription/paywall checks when relevant.
acceptance_checks: A human can run the checklist without asking what to tap.
Every core feature from app_features appears in QA.
Failure states are tested, not ignored.

rules: Prepare launch material and review risk assessment, not marketing fluff.
Treat privacy labels, permission strings, subscriptions, support, and review blockers as required launch work.
Do not mark launch-ready when verification or QA still has blockers.
acceptance_checks: The app has an honest launch-readiness verdict.
Privacy and permissions are specific.
Subscription value and compliance risks are explicit.

rules: Judge the app against the original prompt, the MVP slice, and verification results.
Do not hide unfinished work.
Separate launch blockers from nice-to-have follow-up.
acceptance_checks: The review is honest enough for a user to decide whether to run or iterate.
Every blocker has an owner or a concrete next step.

rules: For portfolio parents, validate the actual folder/project shape against the user's requested app count/categories.
For portfolio children, validate parent metadata and workflow selection.
For single-app runs, explicitly mark the audit not applicable instead of inventing portfolio work.
acceptance_checks: A multi-app parent cannot pass if selected apps were collapsed into one project folder.
Every child has an initial prompt and workflow.
Any mismatch is recorded as a blocker.

rules: Map the target READ-ONLY before hunting; never propose edits in this phase.
Identify languages/framework versions, dependency manifests, entry points, external inputs, and trust boundaries.
Locate where secrets, persistence, and network I/O live, and rank the highest-risk surfaces.
Emit NO findings here — this phase only produces the shared map later phases build on.
required_output: Entry points and external inputs (routes/handlers/CLI/URL schemes).
Trust boundaries and where secrets/persistence live.
Ranked list of highest-risk areas to investigate.
acceptance_checks: A later phase can find each risky surface from this map alone.
No finding-json blocks were emitted yet.
Dependency manifests and versions are enumerated, not guessed.

rules: Hunt real vulnerabilities: injection, broken authn/authz, insecure storage, weak TLS, over-broad permissions, vulnerable deps, PII leaks.
Cite file:line for every claim; a finding without a location is a guess.
Give a concrete exploit scenario and a safe, minimal fix per finding.
Emit each finding as a finding-json block with severity, category, confidence, file, title, fix.
required_output: Exploit scenario and concrete fix per finding.
acceptance_checks: Every finding is reproducible from its file:line + scenario.
No finding restates a guess as fact.
Severity reflects real exploitability, not theoretical risk.

rules: Find correctness/reliability bugs: races, swallowed errors, unhandled edges (nil/empty/off-by-one/overflow/timezone), lifecycle/leak issues, logic errors.
State the input or state that triggers the wrong behavior.
Cite file:line and give a minimal fix.
Emit each as a finding-json block.
acceptance_checks: Each bug has a concrete trigger, not just a code smell.
Fixes are minimal and don't drop features.
Severity matches real user/data impact.

rules: Identify outdated/abandoned deps, deprecated APIs, worthwhile modern-idiom refactors, dead code, and performance issues.
Give current-vs-recommended and the migration effort/risk.
Do not propose churn for its own sake — tie each item to a concrete benefit.
Emit each as a finding-json block.
acceptance_checks: Each recommendation names a concrete benefit.
Breaking-change risk is called out where it exists.
No pure-style churn without payoff.

rules: Synthesize ALL prior findings into ONE prioritized, de-duplicated report; do NOT vote findings away.
Group Critical/High/Medium/Low and open with a 3-line severity-count summary.
End with the top 5 fixes to do first.
The ranked list itself is assembled deterministically by the tool — keep prose honest and non-duplicative.
acceptance_checks: No finding from an earlier phase was dropped.
Duplicates are merged, not repeated.
A reader knows the top 5 things to fix first.

rules: Surface what's known: key facts, the sub-questions that matter, competing viewpoints, and where uncertainty lives.
Separate established facts from claims that need weighing.
Note the source or basis for each significant claim.
Do not conclude yet — this phase collects, the next phase judges.
acceptance_checks: The next phase has enough to weigh the evidence.
Facts and unverified claims are distinguished.
No premature conclusion.

rules: Weigh the evidence, resolve contradictions, and separate strong claims from weak ones.
Decide what the balance of reasoning actually supports.
Name the assumptions behind each conclusion.
Flag where the evidence is thin rather than papering over it.
required_output: Which claims are strong vs weak and why.
acceptance_checks: Conclusions follow from the gathered evidence.
Contradictions are resolved, not ignored.
Uncertainty is stated, not hidden.

rules: Define exactly what 'production-ready' means for THIS prototype: what's missing, what must be real, the acceptance bar.
Distinguish demo shortcuts (mocked data, no auth) from genuine gaps.
Prioritize by risk and user impact, not by ease.
required_output: Inventory of what's mocked/stubbed vs real.
acceptance_checks: A builder knows exactly what 'done' means.
Every demo shortcut is identified.
Scope is bounded, not open-ended.

rules: Design the server: data model, API contracts, service boundaries, and how the client talks to it.
Specify exact endpoint shapes, status codes, and error envelopes.
Choose sessions vs tokens per surface and justify it.
Design for revocation, validation, and least privilege from the start.
required_output: API contract (endpoints, methods, request/response, error shape).
acceptance_checks: The client team could code against the contract as written.
Error and auth behavior are specified, not implied.
Trade-offs are justified.

rules: Decide hosting, deployment, auth, security, observability, and a rough cost model with justified trade-offs.
Name the secrets-management approach — never secrets in code or config committed to git.
Specify how you'll know it's healthy (health checks, logs, metrics) and how you'll roll back.
acceptance_checks: Secrets never live in the repo.
There is a concrete way to detect and roll back a bad deploy.
Cost is estimated, not ignored.

rules: Plan how the prototype consumes the backend, the migration/cutover, and the division of build work with conflict-prevention.
Sequence the work so the app keeps compiling/running at each step.
Name file ownership per lane to prevent merge conflicts.
required_output: Per-lane work division and file ownership.
acceptance_checks: No step leaves the app broken.
Lanes don't contend for the same files.
Cutover success is measurable.

rules: Iteratively build the backend and wire the prototype to it; keep it booting at every iteration.
Expose GET /health returning 200 so the build can be verified by actually booting the server.
Validate all external input; return typed error envelopes, never raw stack traces.
Do not commit secrets or artifacts.
required_output: A server that boots and answers GET /health.
Honest note on any endpoint still stubbed.
acceptance_checks: The server boots and /health returns 200.
Endpoints match the agreed contract.
No secret or artifact was committed.

rules: Assess production readiness: reliability, rollback, security, observability, and a clear go/no-go.
Verify the acceptance bar from assess_prototype is actually met.
State residual risks plainly rather than declaring victory.
required_output: Which acceptance criteria are met vs not.
acceptance_checks: The decision is backed by the acceptance bar, not vibes.
Unmet criteria are named.
Rollback is confirmed to work.

rules: Reason from genuinely different angles; surface the strongest candidate answers and pressure-test them against each other.
Attack the best answer, not a strawman.
Separate what's known from what's assumed.
required_output: The strongest case for and against each.
acceptance_checks: More than one serious answer was weighed.
The leading answer survived a real challenge.
Assumptions are explicit.

rules: Commit to the single best-supported answer and write it clearly.
Note the key reasoning and any honest uncertainty.
Answer the question actually asked — no hedging into non-answers.
acceptance_checks: A reader gets a clear answer, not a menu.
The reasoning supports the answer.
Uncertainty is acknowledged where real.

rules: Read the target repos READ-ONLY; map each one's shape, stack, and the responsibilities they share.
Identify recurring patterns and duplicated concerns across repos.
Emit no extraction proposals yet — this phase maps.
acceptance_checks: Later phases can spot commonality from this map.
No repo was written to.
Duplication is located, not assumed.

rules: Weigh which shared patterns are genuinely reusable vs superficially similar.
Distinguish a real abstraction from coincidental duplication.
Name the cost of extracting each candidate.
required_output: Real-abstraction vs coincidence judgment per pattern.
acceptance_checks: Each candidate has a genuine reuse case.
Coincidental similarity is filtered out.
Cost is weighed, not ignored.

rules: Propose concrete library extraction candidates with a clear interface and the repos that would consume them.
Prefer a small, stable interface over a large speculative one.
Note migration effort and risk per candidate.
acceptance_checks: Each candidate has at least two real consumers.
Interfaces are minimal and stable.
Migration risk is stated.

rules: Scope the feature/fix precisely against the EXISTING app; change the minimum needed.
Identify which existing files/interfaces are affected and what must NOT change.
Define acceptance criteria for the change before building.
acceptance_checks: The change is bounded, not a rewrite.
Existing behavior outside scope is protected.
Done is defined before building.

rules: Write REAL native unit-test unit tests against the app_build code just written — never placeholder/empty tests that only assert true.
Prioritize coverage of core logic and view-models (business rules, data transforms, state machines) over trivial UI snapshot tests.
Add a dedicated test target/scheme if the project doesn't already have one, so the build tool can discover and run it during build verification.
Keep tests deterministic — no network calls, no real timers/sleeps, no reliance on wall-clock or external state.
Do not modify production code to make a test pass; fix the test or file a note if production code looks wrong.
required_output: Which test target/scheme was created or extended.
List of test files added and what each covers.
Any core logic left untested and why.
acceptance_checks: At least one real native unit-testCase file exists under a discoverable test target.
Tests exercise actual app_build types/functions, not stubs.
No test hard-fails immediately from a missing import/target wiring mistake.

rules: Answer the human's most recent message directly before anything else.
Build on or challenge the other agents by name only when it genuinely moves the conversation.
Never fabricate consensus, decisions, or outcomes — this phase has no coordinator and no vote.
Label uncertainty honestly instead of papering over it.
required_output: A direct, concrete response to the human's latest message.
acceptance_checks: The response addresses what the human actually asked, not a restated agenda.
No invented decisions or consensus claims appear.

rules: Fill only the blueprint slots the deterministic render left thin or empty.
Draft every slot from the project's published artifacts and prior-phase decisions — never invent a fact the artifacts don't support.
Where the evidence for a slot is genuinely absent, name the gap; do not write speculative prose to hide it.
required_output: A phase-output-json block whose doc_sections map keys the filled blueprint slots.
Each filled section's markdown, self-contained and finished.
A named list of slots left as gaps for lack of supporting artifacts.
acceptance_checks: Every drafted claim traces to a published artifact or a named phase decision.
No slot is filled with invention; unsupported slots are declared gaps.
The phase-output-json block parses and its doc_sections keys match real blueprint slots.

rules: Read the assembled documentation as one whole; look across sections, not within one.
Flag contradictions, duplicated claims, and passages that read as thin filler.
This is a review, not a rewrite: name each problem and the sections it spans; do not author replacement content.
required_output: A list of contradictions, each naming the sections it spans.
A list of duplicated or redundant passages to merge.
A list of sections still reading as thin or unsupported.
acceptance_checks: Every inconsistency names the specific sections involved.
No new documentation content is invented in this pass.
A section flagged thin is tied to the missing artifact or decision that would resolve it.
